# zladiv

> Performs complex division: out = X / Y, where X and Y are complex.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zladiv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zladiv';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zladiv( x, y, out ) → Complex128Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | `Complex128Array` | Numerator complex number |
| `y` | `Complex128Array` | Denominator complex number |
| `out` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output complex number |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `y`: The complex scalars X and Y.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: result

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zladiv.strided( x, offsetX, y, offsetY, out, offsetOut ) → Complex128Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | `Complex128Array` | Numerator complex number |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset (in complex elements) into x |
| `y` | `Complex128Array` | Denominator complex number |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset (in complex elements) into y |
| `out` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output complex number |
| ↳ `offsetOut` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset (in complex elements) into out |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `y`: The complex scalars X and Y.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: out

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zladiv()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLADIV`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zladiv.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zladiv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zladiv';

// Compute (1+2i) / (3-4i):
const x = new Complex128Array( [ 1.0, 2.0 ] );
const y = new Complex128Array( [ 3.0, -4.0 ] );
const out = new Complex128Array( 1 );

// Using the standard interface:
zladiv( x, y, out );
console.log( reinterpret( out, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the strided interface (operands stored at complex offsets):
const xs = new Complex128Array( [ 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0 ] );
const ys = new Complex128Array( [ 3.0, -4.0 ] );
const outs = new Complex128Array( 2 );
zladiv.strided( xs, 1, ys, 0, outs, 1 );
console.log( reinterpret( outs, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLADIV`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLADIV := X / Y, where X and Y are complex. The computation of X / Y will not overflow on an intermediary step unless the results overflows.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
